tagline: City of monkeys and King Narai's palace, with sunflower fields in the cool season
introHtml:
Lopburi is an old town that brings two things to mind first: the monkeys and King Narai's palace. The old quarter has troops of monkeys roaming the streets around Phra Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan, a sight you won't find anywhere else. Phra Narai Ratchaniwet and Ban Wichayen tell the story of King Narai's reign, when Lopburi served as a second royal capital.

Head a little outside town and the mood changes. In the cool season, big sunflower fields bloom yellow around Phatthana Nikhom district and Khao Chin Lae, and there's the Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, where you can ride the floating train across the water late in the year. The food runs from boat noodles and fresh-coconut khanom piakpoon to the custard apples grown on the hill slopes around Mueang and Phatthana Nikhom districts.
bestTime: November–January, cool weather, sunflowers in full bloom, and the floating train at Pa Sak Dam to ride

highlights.name: Phra Prang Sam Yot and the monkeys
highlights.blurb: A three-towered Khmer temple in the old town overrun with crab-eating macaques. It's the image people picture when they think of Lopburi, and they come to see and photograph it.

highlights.name: Phra Narai Ratchaniwet
highlights.blurb: King Narai's old palace in the heart of town, with throne halls and palace walls to walk through. It's now a museum telling the story of Lopburi.

highlights.name: Sunflower fields
highlights.blurb: In the cool season, wide sunflower fields bloom yellow around Phatthana Nikhom and Khao Chin Lae, a favorite photo spot late in the year.

highlights.name: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
highlights.blurb: A large dam where, late in the year, the floating train runs across the crest. People love riding it to take in the views over the wide reservoir.

highlights.name: San Phra Kan
highlights.blurb: An old shrine paired with Phra Prang Sam Yot, with monkeys living all around it. Locals stop to pay respects and feed the monkeys as a matter of course.

highlights.name: Khao Chin Lae
highlights.blurb: A limestone hill outside town ringed with sunflowers in the cool season, a popular backdrop for photos and a well-liked viewpoint.

foodScene.name: Boat noodles
foodScene.note: Lopburi has several boat-noodle shops in town serving small bowls of strong, dark broth. You order a stack at a time, and it's a popular lunch.

foodScene.name: Lopburi custard apples
foodScene.note: A local specialty grown on the hill slopes in Mueang and Phatthana Nikhom districts. The fruit is large and sweet, and in season you can buy some to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Fresh-coconut khanom piakpoon
foodScene.note: A local sweet you'll find at the markets, soft and topped with fresh coconut cream. It's the town's signature dessert, and people stop to buy it to take home.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are easy to find all over town. The flavors are bold and tasty, an easy meal with plenty of shops to choose from.

foodScene.name: Rice-and-curry and street food in the old quarter
foodScene.note: Around the markets and streets of the old quarter you'll find rice-and-curry shops and snacks to graze on at local prices. Eat before you go walking around the palace and temples.

foodScene.name: Cafes in the old quarter
foodScene.note: The old quarter has small cafes in old buildings and shophouses where you can sit and sip a coffee after walking around the historic sites.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with several shops to choose from at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Shrimp and freshwater fish near Pa Sak Dam
foodScene.note: Riverside restaurants near Pa Sak Jolasid Dam serve fresh shrimp and freshwater fish, eaten with a view over the reservoir.

attractions.name: Phra Prang Sam Yot
attractions.blurb: A three-towered Khmer temple in the old town that's home to a troop of monkeys. It's the lasting image of Lopburi that everyone comes to see.

attractions.name: Phra Narai Ratchaniwet
attractions.blurb: King Narai's old palace, with throne halls and palace walls to walk through. It's now a national museum.

attractions.name: Ban Wichayen
attractions.blurb: The ruins of a nobleman's house from King Narai's reign that mixes in European construction. Walk among the old brickwork and arches.

attractions.name: San Phra Kan
attractions.blurb: An old shrine paired with Phra Prang Sam Yot, with monkeys all around. People stop to pay respects and feed the monkeys as a matter of course.

attractions.name: Phatthana Nikhom sunflower fields
attractions.blurb: Wide sunflower fields that bloom yellow in the cool season, a popular photo spot around Phatthana Nikhom district.

attractions.name: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
attractions.blurb: A large dam where the floating train runs across the crest late in the year. You can take in the views over the wide reservoir at an easy pace.

attractions.name: Khao Chin Lae
attractions.blurb: A limestone hill outside town ringed with sunflowers in the cool season, a backdrop for photos and a viewpoint.

attractions.name: Wild sunflower fields and hill viewpoints
attractions.blurb: The hill slopes on the Phatthana Nikhom side have viewpoints and seasonal flower fields, a good stop for photos on the way to the dam.
